Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Several week history of left knee pain after fall. Pain localized laterally. No prior surgery.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Mild degenerative subchondral cystic change at the anterior margin of the medial tibial plateau. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. 

JOINT SPACE:
Minimal joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Oblique undersurface tear involving the posterior body-horn junction and posterior horn medial meniscus with superimposed small 3 mm intrameniscal cyst formation of the posterior horn. Moderate extrusion of the body partially displaced within the meniscotibial recess.
Medial compartment cartilage: Scattered areas of low grade partial thickness cartilage loss along the central weightbearing medial femoral condyle and along the anterior medial tibial plateau.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the anterior weightbearing lateral femoral condyle.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss involving the lateral patellar facet. Trochlear cartilage remains intact.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Intact.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Grade 2 sprain of the fibular collateral ligament proximally near the femoral attachment characterized by high-grade partial-thickness tearing and fiber irregularity and surrounding peritendinous edema. The iliotibial band, biceps femoris and popliteus tendon are intact. Popliteofibular ligament appears intact.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 8 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Moderate prepatellar subcutaneous soft tissue edema and non organized fluid, may reflect underlying soft tissue contusion in the setting of fall. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	High-grade 2 sprain involving the proximal fibular collateral ligament, remaining posterolateral corner structures are intact.
2.	Oblique undersurface tear posterior body and posterior horn medial meniscus with moderate meniscal extrusion and partial displacement within the meniscotibial recess.
3.	Mild tricompartmental chondrosis.
4.	Small Baker cyst.
5.	Moderate anterior soft tissue edema likely representing contusion.
